measures.questionText: Shall the following ordinance be adopted? **An Ordinance of the City of Emporia, Kansas Prohibiting the Installation and Operation of High Impact Data Centers**
measures.officialStatement: Explanatory Statement: This ordinance would prohibit the construction, installation, operation, and maintenance of High Impact Data Centers within the City of Emporia, Kansas. A "High Impact Data Center" is defined as a facility whose primary purpose is the housing, operation, and maintenance of computer servers and related infrastructure that requires a peak electrical load exceeding ten (10) megawatts or a daily water draw exceeding one hundred thousand (100,000) gallons. This term includes server farms, colocation facilities, Al training facilities, cryptocurrency mining operations, and similar high-density computing facilities. The prohibition would apply to all zoning districts within the City. Violations would be subject to civil and criminal penalties under the City of Emporia Zoning Regulations.

measures.questionText: Shall the following ordinance be adopted? **An Ordinance of the City of Emporia, Kansas Prohibiting the Installation and Operation of Type 2 and Type 3 Battery Energy Storage Systems**
measures.officialStatement: Explanatory Statement: This ordinance would prohibit the construction, installation, operation, and maintenance of Tier 2 and Tier 3 Battery Energy Storage Systems ("BESS") within the City of Emporia, Kansas. A Tier 2 BESS is a battery energy storage system with an aggregate energy capacity between 81 and 600 kWh, and a Tier 3 BESS is a battery energy storage system with an aggregate energy capacity greater than 600 kWh. The prohibition would apply to all zoning districts within the City. Violations would be subject to civil and criminal penalties under Article 15 of the City of Emporia Zoning Regulations.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorizes a new 0.25% city sales tax to buy, build and equip a recreation facility and pay for other recreation improvements and quality-of-life projects, including debt payments for those projects. Collection would begin April 1, 2027, or as soon afterward as the law allows. The question gives no end date.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the 0.25% city sales tax for these projects and related financing.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this proposed sales tax.

parts.label: Use and duration
parts.what: The calling resolution classifies this as a general-purpose sales tax. It authorizes spending on the listed projects and debt service, and reimbursement of other city funds used for those projects. Neither the question nor the operative resolution sets an expiration date.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Prohibits covered high-impact data centers throughout Emporia. It covers facilities mainly used for bulk data processing, storage or transmission that need more than 10 megawatts of peak electricity or draw more than 100,000 gallons of water daily. Ordinary office servers, school computer labs and manufacturing controls that are secondary to a building’s main use are excluded. The calling resolution makes enactment conditional on court authorization; a yes vote alone would not make it take effect.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the proposed data-center ban, subject to the calling resolution’s court-authorization condition.

parts.label: Court condition
parts.what: Resolution 3799 says an approved ordinance cannot be published or enacted until the Lyon County District Court finds it valid under the cited initiative law or issues a further order. This describes the official resolution’s condition; no later court decision is asserted here.

parts.label: Citywide application and enforcement
parts.what: The proposed ordinance applies in all city zoning districts and land-use categories. Violations would face existing civil and criminal penalties in Article 15 of the City zoning regulations. A no vote rejects this ordinance; other existing zoning requirements would continue to apply.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Prohibits Tier 2 and Tier 3 battery-storage systems throughout Emporia. These categories cover systems with 81–600 kilowatt-hours of capacity, larger systems, and rooms or enclosed areas using more than one storage technology. The ordinance also treats some combinations of smaller systems as prohibited larger systems. Stand-alone 12-volt car batteries and electric vehicles are excluded.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Adopt the ordinance prohibiting the covered battery-storage systems, subject to applicable law and court orders.

parts.label: Definition omitted from the shorter statement
parts.what: The official explanatory statement describes Tier 2 by its 81–600 kilowatt-hour range. The full proposed ordinance also classifies a room or enclosed area using more than one storage technology as Tier 2, without stating a minimum capacity for that alternative. Tier 3 generally covers capacity above 600 kilowatt-hours.

parts.label: Smaller systems and combinations
parts.what: Single-technology systems of 80 kilowatt-hours or less can remain subject to applicable codes. Several smaller systems cannot be arranged to function as a prohibited larger system. Factors include total capacity, shared equipment or controls, integrated operation and proximity on the same or commonly controlled adjacent parcels.

parts.label: Scope, penalties and legal review
parts.what: The ban would apply in all city zoning districts and land-use categories, with existing Article 15 civil and criminal zoning penalties. Resolution 3800 preserves the City’s ability to seek judicial review. It does not contain the same express pre-enactment court-authorization condition as the separate data-center resolution.
